solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Islander very good on horse you say? Not so

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is placed after it
'you say' asks the solver to hear the horse word spoken rather than spell it

parts.note: a filly is a young female horse
PI, short for pious, is crosswordese for very good
to say something is not so is to say no

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an island-dweller was a fine rider, and gets told otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you say' makes only the horse word spoken, its double L heard as one; 'Not so' is a flat denial.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Philippines, an island nation, is called a Filipino.

clue.text: F1 celebrity

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or dice

explanation.surface: A Formula One racing star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'F1' reads as Formula One motor racing, but splits into F and 1.
explanation.definitionFit: A face is a well-known person, as in a famous face on television.

clue.text: Officer in India, about to leave, as it happens

indicators.note: to leave means this letter departs from the officer's name

parts.note: Robert Clive, Clive of India, was a British officer in India
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: An officer serving in India is about to go home, just as it is happening.
explanation.definitionFit: A live broadcast is shown in real time, as events take place.

clue.text: Poor writer taking river boat

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
the Nile is the river of Egypt
SS, steamship, prefixes ship names

explanation.surface: A struggling author takes a boat up the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Penniless means having no money at all, so very poor.

clue.text: Men hitch a lift into Scottish town, going north from Durham area?

indicators.note: into means the following pieces go inside the town name
in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Nairn is a town in the Scottish Highlands
OR, other ranks, means enlisted men
to thumb a ride is to hitch a lift

explanation.surface: Soldiers hitchhike into a Scottish town, travelling north from County Durham.
explanation.walkthrough: Durham is a county in north-east England, within the old kingdom of Northumbria; the question mark marks this as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Northumbrian means belonging to Northumbria, the north-east English region that includes Durham.

clue.text: Parisian who is admitted into play free?

indicators.note: being admitted into something means going inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a play has acts; act can mean to play or perform
qui is the French word for who, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A question about letting someone into a theatre performance without paying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like 'free admission' but it is a verb: to clear someone in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquit a defendant is to set them free by verdict of not guilty.

clue.text: Fall asleep in Lycra shorts

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone nods off wearing cycling shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Crash is slang for going to sleep, as in crash out.

clue.text: Upper-class celebrity in car, breaking down like a Cadillac? Hardly

parts.note: U denotes upper-class usage in British English
a name, a big name, is a celebrity

indicators.note: breaking down suggests a car falling apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A posh star whose car breaks down: not much like a smooth Cadillac.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cadillac is quintessentially American, so 'Hardly' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not at all like an American car is un-American, alien to the United States.

clue.text: Rations tin for building bridge

indicators.note: building means constructing something new from these letters

explanation.surface: Tinned rations are used to construct a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge in music or argument is a passage linking two parts, a transition.

clue.text: City firm opening railway

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A company starts operating a railway line in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Coventry is a city in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Mother meeting grandmother later

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
nana is a familiar name for a grandmother

explanation.surface: Mum will see Granny some time afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish mañana, tomorrow, is used in English for some indefinite future time.

clue.text: Party politician certain to conceal old state of anxiety

indicators.note: to conceal means the pieces hide the short letter inside them

parts.note: a disco is a dance party
MP, member of parliament, is a politician
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A party politician sure to hide the past in an anxious state.
explanation.definitionFit: Discomposure is agitation, the loss of calm that anxiety brings.

clue.text: Felt tip pens less important in secondary schools

indicators.note: in places the comparative word inside the plural schools word

parts.note: high schools, informally highs, are secondary schools
lighter, as in a lighter matter, means less weighty or important

explanation.surface: Felt-tip pens are of little consequence in secondary schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Highlighters are broad felt-tipped pens used to mark text in bright colour.

clue.text: Reserve shown by bright fellow touring distant island

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the fellow's word surrounds the others

parts.note: a spark, bright spark, is a lively clever person
afar means at a distance

explanation.surface: A clever man shows reserve while touring a remote island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' suggests restraint but is a nature reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari park is an enclosed reserve where wild animals roam for visitors to drive through.

clue.text: Particular Lenten activity sounding 'orrendous

parts.note: fasting is the traditional observance of Lent

indicators.note: sounding means the following word is taken as heard, not spelt

parts.note: horrendous with its h dropped suggests hideous said with a dropped h

explanation.surface: Someone with a dropped-h accent calls the strict Lent observance horrendous.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped h of 'orrendous signals that the synonym hideous also loses its h.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastidious means fussy, very particular about details or cleanliness.

clue.text: Group mostly admitted into A & E quickly

indicators.note: something admitted into a place goes inside it

parts.note: taken as the letters A and E

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a pack is a group, as of wolves or cards

explanation.surface: A crowd is rushed into the hospital's accident and emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: A & E is the British hospital emergency department; here it just supplies A and E around PAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an old adverb meaning at speed, swiftly.

clue.text: A feature film covers factory worker

indicators.note: covers means the film word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on glass
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A movie depicts a factory worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature film' reads as a movie, but 'feature' is the chin and 'film' is a mist.
explanation.definitionFit: A machinist operates machines in a factory or workshop.

clue.text: Involve rogue and spiteful woman in deceit

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rogue

indicators.note: in puts the woman inside the word for deceit

parts.note: a lie is a deceit
cat is a term for a spiteful woman

explanation.surface: A scoundrel and a malicious woman are drawn into a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: To implicate someone is to show them to be involved in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Plant containing source of this unusual medical treatment

indicators.note: the plant name holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: anise is an aromatic plant

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or unusual

explanation.surface: A plant that contains the origin of this odd remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' looks like an anagram signal but is the slang word rum; 'source of' takes T, the first letter of 'this'.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiserum is blood serum containing antibodies, given as a medical remedy against disease or venom.

clue.text: Foreign gallery's public relations hoo-ha

parts.note: ado is fuss or commotion, a hoo-ha

explanation.surface: A fuss over publicity at an overseas art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prado in Madrid is Spain's national art museum, a gallery abroad to a British reader.

clue.text: Power seized by one revolutionary in old Asian city

indicators.note: a thing seized by another is held inside it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Power was taken by a single rebel in an ancient city of Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old Asian city' looks like the definition, but 'in old Asian' is anagram fodder with I; P goes inside the rearranged INDIANAOLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Indianapolis is the state capital of Indiana, a US city.

clue.text: Stand bachelor up on unfortunate date, in brief

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a bachelor's degree

indicators.note: in brief means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: the Ides of March was Julius Caesar's fatal date

explanation.surface: A single man is stood up on a disastrous date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' sounds like standing someone up but means tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to stand or tolerate it.

clue.text: Even sections of freezable material

indicators.note: even sections means the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters

explanation.surface: Portions of freezer-safe stuff divided evenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Material, as in material evidence, means real, actual or substantial.

clue.text: Fly before end of late spring

parts.note: to travel through the air by aircraft, a short verb for flying

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Take a flight before spring is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeté is a ballet leap, a spring from one foot to the other.

clue.text: Not stressed a great deal: largely very cool

parts.note: tons, or a ton, is a great deal

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, dropping its final letter

parts.note: ice is very cold, so very cool

explanation.surface: Someone not worried much, being mostly ice-cool.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics an atonic syllable is unaccented, carrying no stress.

clue.text: A joint's picked up by fellow from S America

parts.note: guy is an informal word for a man or fellow

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the words are taken by their spoken sound

parts.note: the knee is a joint, so this says a knee's

explanation.surface: A man picks up a shared cannabis cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a spliff but is the knee; the silent K vanishes when the phrase is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Guyanese describes people or things belonging to Guyana, a country in South America.

clue.text: Strict diet really impresses female

parts.note: to knock someone out, KO them, is to impress them greatly
her is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A rigorous eating plan is a real hit with a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping kosher means observing Jewish dietary law, a strict set of food rules.

clue.text: Party goer finally dropping off? One's received wake-up call

indicators.note: the shortened word receives the numeral, taking it inside
the final letter of the reveller word drops off

parts.note: a reveller is someone who goes to parties
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A partygoer finally falls asleep, then gets an alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping off' suggests nodding off but means the last letter, R, is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle signal sounded to wake soldiers in the morning.
